name: Intuition
oracle_text: Search your library for three cards and reveal them. Target opponent chooses one. Put that card into your hand and the rest into your graveyard. Then shuffle.
blocked_sentences: Put that card into your hand and the rest into your graveyard.

needs.what: a `chooser` on `search_library`/`search_zones` (a player spec, so it can be `{"target": ...}`) naming who picks from among the cards the search turned up -- the search itself is still performed and seen by the library's owner, but a *different*, targeted player makes the selection out of the revealed pool. Gifts Ungiven, Intuition and Plea for Power's kin all hang on it
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `_search` (src/commanderblitz/engine/effects/ops_cards.py:208) hardcodes the asker: it iterates `select_players(ctx, spec.get("player", "you"))` and passes that same `pid` into `ask_objects(ctx, prompt, pool, 0, take, pid, "search")`, so the searcher is always the chooser. The selector's `chooser` key exists (selectors.py:850, and it accepts an arbitrary player spec) but a search never routes its selector through `pick_from_pool` -- the selector is only a match test via `_matches_in_zone` -- so writing `chooser` on a search's selector is silently ignored and the caster would pick their own card, which is the entire card. `two_piles` (ops_cards.py:1339) is the only op whose first decision belongs to somebody else, and its splitter is `ctx.opponents()[0]` rather than a target, it reads `library[:amount]` off the top instead of a searched pool, and the *controller* still decides which pile is taken -- the opposite of "target opponent chooses one".
